title: Medication reconciliation policy
body: All care transitions require comparing home, inpatient, and discharge medication lists. Discrepancies (omissions, dose changes, duplicates, new starts) must be resolved or explicitly acknowledged by a licensed clinician or pharmacist before the record is considered complete. JIVANA surfaces discrepancies; it never auto-approves orders.

title: Human-in-the-loop standard
body: AI-generated summaries and extractions are assistive only. Reviewers must verify source blocks on uploaded documents. Items in the review queue require a documented acknowledgment note. Weak or vertex-only evidence always routes to needs_review even when lists appear to match.

title: Document intake requirements
body: Production intake uses Document AI for OCR and layout blocks, then Vertex Gemini for classification and structured medication extraction with source_block_id citations. Upload 1–3 files per reconciliation job: prior list, discharge summary, and current prescription when available.

title: FHIR export after sign-off
body: After human review completes, reconciled outcomes export as a FHIR Bundle (DetectedIssue, MedicationStatement, Provenance) to the configured Cloud Healthcare API FHIR store for audit and downstream EHR integration.

title: Demo and privacy
body: Public demos use synthetic documents only. Do not upload real patient identifiers to hackathon environments. Firebase Auth scopes jobs and activity to the signed-in user when auth is enabled.
